typography.usage_rules: Use for the countdown timer. Letterspacing is critical: use tracking-widest for the countdown labels.

visual enhancers.grain_overlay: An absolute positioned div covering the screen with a subtle noise background and mix-blend-overlay to give a cinematic film feel.
visual enhancers.vignette: A bottom-heavy linear gradient `bg-gradient-to-t from-black/80 via-black/20 to-transparent` to ensure the countdown text is legible against the golden-hour background.
visual enhancers.separators: Use 1px thin borders `border-[#C5A059]/30` between the countdown units.

grids.bento_grid: Not applicable for this single-screen poster design.
grids.layout_grid: Absolute positioning system over a full-screen base.

layouts.container: Single screen, full viewport height (h-screen, w-screen, overflow-hidden). No scrollbars.
layouts.background: Absolute full-bleed image behind all content.
layouts.content_placement: Countdown should be placed in the bottom center of the screen, anchored elegantly (e.g., bottom-12 or bottom-24) so it doesn't obstruct the center.

motion.load_sequence: On mount, the page should slowly fade in from black (duration: 1.5s to 2s).
motion.background_image: Very subtle, slow continuous scale-down: start at scale: 1.05, animate to 1.0 over 10 seconds with ease-out.
motion.countdown_reveal: Staggered fade-up (y: 10, opacity: 0 to 1) for the countdown digits after the background appears.

accessibility.aria_labels: Ensure the countdown timer has clear aria-labels for screen readers.
accessibility.contrast: The dark vignette gradient guarantees the gold text meets WCAG AA contrast against any background image.

media.strategy: Full-bleed background image simulating a movie poster. User will provide the actual image, but a fallback is provided.

3d libraries.usage: None. Keep it 2D and cinematic. Framer Motion is sufficient for the cinematic fades and scaling.

steps: 1. Setup the full-screen container with overflow hidden.
2. Add the background image with object-cover and Framer Motion scale animation.
3. Add the grain and vignette overlays.
4. Implement the countdown logic targeting September 1, 2026.
5. Style the countdown with gold serif typography and stagger its entrance.

background_fallback.description: Fallback golden-hour countryside background image. Use this in the background URL.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly build a ONE-PAGE, ONE-SCREEN website (h-screen, overflow-hidden). Do not add a scrollable layout or additional sections.
The user explicitly requested: 'dont add anything just use the image'. Do NOT render the large text blocks or logos in HTML. The text is already part of the user's poster image.
Your ONLY tasks are: 1. Render the full-screen background image. 2. Apply cinematic overlays (grain and vignette). 3. Build and position the elegant countdown timer.
Implement the countdown timer targeting September 2026. Use the gold accent color (text-[#C5A059]) and serif typography.
Add a cinematic fade-in on load using Framer Motion.
Do NOT add a standard navigation bar. This is a pure cinematic coming-soon poster screen.
Ensure the countdown has data-testid='countdown-timer' and other interactive or key elements have appropriate data-testid attributes.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, and transition animations separate good from extraordinary.
NEVER use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Do not use generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a data-testid attribute (e.g., data-testid='countdown-days').
